questions.question: Which framework explains major contributors to VTE risk?
choices: Virchow's triad of stasis, endothelial injury, and hypercoagulability
The Glasgow Coma Scale
The ABCDE allergy framework
The osteoarthritis pain ladder
questions.explanation: Virchow's triad organizes VTE risk: stasis, endothelial injury, and hypercoagulability. It helps structure history but does not replace diagnostic evaluation.

questions.question: A patient has sudden dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, syncope, and hypotension. What is the best disposition?
choices: Routine outpatient D-dimer testing
Emergency evaluation for possible high-risk PE and other life-threatening causes
Start an exercise program
Reassure because PE always causes leg swelling first
questions.explanation: Hypotension, syncope, and severe respiratory symptoms indicate possible hemodynamic instability. Emergency transport and resuscitation-capable evaluation are required.

questions.question: What is the best interpretation of a positive D-dimer result?
choices: It confirms PE
It confirms DVT
It is nonspecific and requires interpretation within a pretest-probability diagnostic pathway
It means anticoagulation can be stopped
questions.explanation: D-dimer is often elevated for many reasons. A positive result does not diagnose VTE; it must be interpreted with clinical probability and followed by appropriate imaging when indicated.

questions.question: Which symptom is least reliable for excluding DVT when absent?
choices: Unilateral leg swelling
Calf tenderness
Warmth
All of these can be absent despite DVT
questions.explanation: DVT can have few or no symptoms. No single examination finding can safely exclude it when clinical probability is concerning.

questions.question: A patient on anticoagulation reports black stool and lightheadedness. What is the best FNP response?
choices: Wait until the next routine follow-up
Treat as possible clinically significant bleeding and arrange urgent evaluation
Double the next anticoagulant dose
Tell the patient to take an NSAID for stomach discomfort
questions.explanation: Melena with lightheadedness may indicate significant gastrointestinal bleeding. Urgent evaluation is needed; medication decisions must occur within a safety assessment.

questions.question: Why is a normal resting oxygen saturation insufficient to exclude PE?
choices: PE never affects oxygenation
Patients with PE can have normal saturation, especially early or at rest
Oxygen saturation determines anticoagulant dose
Pulse oximetry only measures venous oxygen
questions.explanation: PE has variable presentation. Normal saturation does not rule out PE, and probability-based assessment remains necessary.

questions.question: Which question is essential at a follow-up visit for a patient taking a direct oral anticoagulant?
choices: Whether they prefer a different tablet color
Indication, dose, duration, kidney function when relevant, bleeding, missed doses, interactions, and upcoming procedures
Only whether leg pain is gone
Whether they own a blood pressure cuff
questions.explanation: Anticoagulation safety requires a complete medication-system review, including indication, dosing, organ function, interactions, adherence, bleeding, and procedural plans.

questions.question: A patient has persistent dyspnea months after PE. What is the best clinical approach?
choices: Assume it is always deconditioning
Reassess for post-PE complications and alternative cardiopulmonary causes
Stop all follow-up because the clot was treated
Start antibiotics without assessment
questions.explanation: Persistent or progressive symptoms after PE merit evaluation for complications such as chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension and for other cardiopulmonary diagnoses.

questions.question: Which factor can change the appropriate anticoagulant pathway and warrants specialty-informed coordination?
choices: Pregnancy or postpartum status
A stable shoe size
Seasonal allergies alone
A remote uncomplicated cold
questions.explanation: Pregnancy and postpartum state change diagnostic and anticoagulation considerations. Coordinate promptly with obstetrics and appropriate specialists.

questions.question: What does it mean to use testing according to pretest probability in suspected VTE?
choices: Order every test for every patient
Use history, examination, risk, and validated pathways to choose D-dimer, imaging, or emergency evaluation
Avoid imaging in high-risk patients
Use D-dimer as the only rule-out test regardless of risk
questions.explanation: Pretest probability guides efficient and safe testing. High-risk or unstable patients often need urgent imaging or emergency evaluation rather than a D-dimer-first strategy.
